# Fix notes: `slugify` produced repeated and trailing hyphens

## Root cause

`slugify` used `re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]", "-", text)`, which replaces **each**
non-alphanumeric character with its own hyphen. A run like `",  "` (comma plus
two spaces) became `"---"`, and trailing punctuation such as `"!"` left a
dangling `"-"`. So `slugify("Hello,  World!")` returned `"hello---world-"`.

## Fix

In `textutils.py`:

- Changed the pattern to `[^a-z0-9]+` so that each run of non-alphanumeric
  characters collapses into a single hyphen.
- Added `.strip("-")` so the result has no leading or trailing hyphens.
- Added type hints (`text: str -> str`), following the project conventions.

Input that has no alphanumeric characters at all (e.g. `"!!!"`) now returns
`""`.

## Test

Added regression tests to `tests/test_textutils.py`:

- `test_regression_slugify_collapses_separators`: the case from the report,
  `"Hello,  World!"` → `"hello-world"`.
- `test_regression_slugify_strips_edge_separators`: leading and trailing
  hyphens and punctuation are removed.
- `test_regression_slugify_only_punctuation`: input with only punctuation, and
  empty input, both give `""`.

All three failed before the fix. After the fix, all six tests pass with
`python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`.
